gaps.sentence: She works in ___ insurance, not banking.
gaps.explanation: Industry/sector names take no article: in insurance, in banking, in marketing.

gaps.sentence: He plays ___ violin in the youth orchestra.
The thief was sent to ___ prison for three years.
gaps.explanation: 'Sent to prison' — the institution, no article; 'the prison' would mean the building.

gaps.sentence: ___ life in the countryside is much quieter.
gaps.explanation: 'Life' in a general sense takes no article: Life is hard sometimes.

gaps.sentence: He was elected ___ chairman of the board.
gaps.explanation: No article is used with unique roles after 'elect', 'appoint', 'become'.

gaps.sentence: The novel had a huge effect on ___ young people of the 1960s.
gaps.explanation: 'The young people of the 1960s' — defined by the of-phrase, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: They elected her ___ chairperson for a second term.
gaps.explanation: After 'elect/appoint', roles take no article: elected her chairperson.

gaps.sentence: She goes to ___ school by bus every morning.
gaps.explanation: 'Go to school/work/bed/church' (as participant) takes no article.
